questions.q: What does Horizontal Discovery do, per this lesson?
options: Scans broadly across many infrastructure types at once to build general CMDB coverage
Goes deep on exactly one application's dependency chain only
Only scans network switches, never servers or databases
Replaces the need for any Discovery Schedule
questions.explain: Horizontal Discovery is the broad, general-purpose sweep across many infrastructure types.

questions.q: What does Vertical Discovery do, and what is it closely related to?
options: It goes deep on one specific application or service, tracing its full dependency chain — closely related to Service Mapping from Chapter 2
It scans the broadest possible range of IP addresses with no focus on any one service
It is unrelated to any other capability covered earlier in this course
It only identifies operating systems, never dependency relationships
questions.explain: Vertical Discovery traces one service's dependency chain end to end, which is exactly what Service Mapping does.

questions.q: Why would a CMDB program that only ran Horizontal Discovery have a gap?
options: It would know what infrastructure exists broadly but have no reliable dependency map for any specific critical service
Horizontal Discovery cannot find any infrastructure at all
It would have perfect dependency maps but no general infrastructure coverage
There is no gap — Horizontal Discovery alone is always sufficient
questions.explain: Horizontal Discovery builds general coverage but doesn't trace any one service's specific dependency chain — that's Vertical Discovery's job.

questions.q: When would Vertical Discovery be the right tool to use, per this lesson?
options: When the goal is understanding exactly how one specific, important application is built, tracing it through every tier it touches
When the goal is building baseline infrastructure coverage across an entire environment
Only when no MID Server is available
Vertical Discovery is never the right tool in practice
questions.explain: Vertical Discovery is for precise, deep dependency mapping of one business-critical service, not broad coverage.

questions.q: Why do real CMDB programs typically need both Horizontal and Vertical Discovery?
options: They answer different questions — broad general coverage versus a precise dependency map for one critical service
Because ServiceNow requires both to be enabled even if only one is ever used
Because Vertical Discovery is simply a faster version of Horizontal Discovery
Because Horizontal Discovery cannot run without Vertical Discovery first
questions.explain: Horizontal Discovery answers "what do we have broadly," while Vertical Discovery answers "what does this one critical service depend on, precisely" — distinct, complementary questions.
